title: Circular ring
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero degrees and the translation vector also set to zero. This ensures that the coordinate system aligns with the default global axes. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, create the first loop by drawing a circle with its center at coordinates [0.375, 0.375] and a radius of 0.375 units. Then, draw the second loop by adding another circle with the same center but a smaller radius of 0.3324 units. After completing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to reduce its size proportionally. Ensure that the sketch remains centered at the original coordinates after scaling. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.008 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The extrusion should only occur in one direction, and the operation should result in a new solid body. The final dimensions of the circular ring with a flat surface are a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.75 units, and a height of 0.007989875230108407 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").center(0.375, 0.375)

# Create the outer circle
sketch = sketch.circle(0.375)

# Create the inner circle
sketch = sketch.circle(0.3324)

# Extrude the sketch to create the ring
extrusion_depth = 0.008
r = sketch.extrude(extrusion_depth)

# Display the result

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the outer circle
outer_circle = workplane.center(0.375, 0.375).circle(0.375)

# Create the inner circle
inner_circle = outer_circle.circle(0.335)

# Extrude the sketch to create the ring
ring = inner_circle.extrude(0.008)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = ring

    cq.Workplane("XY")

    .circle(inner_radius)
